s1.syndrome_frame: Acute spinal cord syndrome with rapid progression of neurological deficits following a surgical procedure
salient_findings: Development of hypesthesia below chest level
Reduction in muscle strength of both lower limbs progressing to flaccid paralysis
Space-occupying lesion at left epidural site with spinal compression
key_facts: No history of gestational diabetes mellitus, preeclampsia, or coagulation disorders
Emergency cesarean section due to amniotic fluid turbidity
Initial recovery of sensation and muscle strength in right lower limb
Mild soreness and swelling with MMT grade of 2 in left lower limb
MRI findings of space-occupying lesion at left epidural site

shortlist.label: Epidural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Acute spinal cord syndrome with rapid progression of neurological deficits following a surgical procedure and presence of space-occupying lesion at left epidural site

shortlist.label: Vascular malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed presence of vascular malformation and spinal compression with rightward shift

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Acute spinal cord syndrome with rapid progression of neurological deficits and presence of space-occupying lesion at left epidural site

shortlist.label: Spinal cord infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of neurological deficits and presence of spinal compression with rightward shift

shortlist.label: Arteriovenous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of vascular malformation and spinal compression with rightward shift

raw.rationale: The patient's development of hypesthesia below chest level, reduction in muscle strength of both lower limbs, and progression to flaccid paralysis after a cesarean section, combined with MRI findings of a space-occupying lesion at the left epidural site causing spinal compression, are highly suggestive of an epidural hematoma.

rejected.label: Vascular malformation
rejected.why: Although a vascular malformation is mentioned in the pathological examination, the acute onset of neurological symptoms and the specific MRI findings are more consistent with an epidural hematoma.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: There is no mention of infection or abscess in the provided information, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Spinal cord infarction
rejected.why: The presence of a space-occupying lesion and spinal compression on MRI suggests a mechanical cause rather than an infarction.

rejected.label: Arteriovenous malformation
rejected.why: While an arteriovenous malformation could cause neurological symptoms, the acute presentation and specific findings are more indicative of an epidural hematoma.
